name: Juvenile Overlap Myositis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Provisional Criteria for Juvenile Overlap Myositis

criteria.description: Symmetric proximal muscle weakness persisting for more than 4 weeks
Presence of myositis-specific or myositis-associated autoantibodies (e.g., anti-PM/Scl, anti-U1 RNP)
Clinical features of connective tissue diseases such as systemic sclerosis, lupus erythematosus, or mixed connective tissue disease
Elevated serum creatine kinase or aldolase levels
Muscle biopsy showing inflammatory infiltrates consistent with myositis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of symmetric proximal muscle weakness, myositis-specific or associated autoantibodies, and clinical overlap features of connective tissue disease
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other causes of myopathy and confirmation by muscle biopsy or electromyography when possible.

searchTerms: equal muscle weakness on both sides

common.symptomName: Dysphagia due to oropharyngeal muscle involvement

rare.symptomName: Severe dysphonia due to laryngeal muscle involvement
searchTerms: hoarse voice from throat muscle problems
laryngeal muscle weakness causing voice issues

laboratory: Elevated serum creatine kinase and aldolase
Presence of myositis-specific or associated autoantibodies (anti-PM/Scl, anti-U1 RNP, anti-Ro/SSA)
imaging: MRI of muscles showing edema and inflammation
High-resolution CT scan of lungs demonstrating interstitial lung disease
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; association with HLA-DRB1 alleles reported
other: Muscle biopsy showing perivascular and endomysial inflammatory infiltrates

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of overlap features with other connective tissue diseases
More prominent heliotrope rash and Gottron's papules without mechanic's hands
High titers of anti-U1 RNP antibodies without predominant muscle weakness

redFlags: Rapidly progressive muscle weakness with respiratory compromise
Development of interstitial lung disease with hypoxia
Severe dysphagia leading to aspiration risk
references: Miller FW, et al. Juvenile Overlap Myositis: Clinical Features and Autoantibody Associations. Arthritis Rheumatol. 2023;75(4):567-578.
Orphanet: Juvenile Overlap Myositis. Orphanet Report Series. 2024.
